# The working life of Sītā: from the myths to the modern trades
Archetypes are not metaphors; they are job descriptions written early. **Sītā**'s was unusually clear.

The Rāmāyaṇa calls itself Rāma's story, but its moral engine is Sītā: every choice that matters is measured against her.

The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) — which maps every flagship temple to the industries its archetype demonstrably resonates with, each match argued and open to challenge — seats this temple in **5 industries**. This file reads those seats the way they were earned: through the myths.
## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Sītā
- **Pantheon:** Sanskrit
- **Domain of influence:** Virtue, Devotion, Fertility
- **Pattern seats:** 5
- **Sectors touched:** Society & Spirit · Home & Lifestyle · Energy & Natural World · Commerce & Governance
- **Strongest seat:** Faith & Spiritual Organizations
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 225 of 271
## The Myth at Work

**Daughter of the Field.** King Janaka of Mithilā, ploughing a sacrificial field, struck something that was not stone: an infant in the furrow, whom he named Sītā — "furrow" — and raised as his daughter.  Earth-born, not womb-born, the texts insist: her mother is the field itself, and the Rāmāyaṇa's most beloved heroine begins as a gift of agriculture. — hold that image; the industries below are where it goes to work.

**The Golden Deer.** In the forest of Daṇḍaka, during the fourteen-year exile, the demon Mārīca became a golden deer to draw Rāma from her side, and Rāvaṇa came as a wandering ascetic.  She crossed the line — the lakṣmaṇa-rekhā drawn for her protection — only to give alms, and was carried through the sky to Laṅkā. — remember the shape of that act. You will see it again, wearing a logo.
## The Seats

Each of these is argued in the atlas with a weight and a why-line. What the atlas cannot fit in one line is the whole myth — so here is each seat with its story restored.

### Faith & Spiritual Organizations

*Religious institutions, faith media, and devotional services. (Sector: Society & Spirit)*

*The furrow-born princess of the Rāmāyaṇa, worshipped beside Rāma as the measure of devotion — virtue enthroned in living temples.* — the atlas stops there, out of discipline. The myth keeps going: the function Sītā performs in the stories is precisely the function this industry sells.

### Wedding, Family & Maternity

*Weddings, childcare, and family services. (Sector: Home & Lifestyle)*

*The Rāmāyaṇa’s devoted wife, whose fidelity survived fire — the Hindu ideal of the marriage bond personified.* Swap the costume and the sentence is indistinguishable from the myth. That is what a resonance seat means.

### Agriculture, Food & Harvest

*Farming, grain, food production, and agtech. (Sector: Energy & Natural World)*

The why-line says it in one breath: *Her name is the furrow; the Ṛgveda prays to her for crops.* That is not a resemblance; it is the same act, performed in a newer building.

### Education, Research & Knowledge

*Schools, universities, and research institutions. (Sector: Society & Spirit)*

*The field-goddess of the Ṛgveda's ploughing hymns; patience as curriculum.* Swap the costume and the sentence is indistinguishable from the myth. That is what a resonance seat means.

### Ancestry & Heritage Services

*Genealogy, heritage research, and DNA ancestry. (Sector: Commerce & Governance)*

*Mother of Lava and Kuśa; the Rāmāyaṇa's own lineage-mother.* — the atlas stops there, out of discipline. The myth keeps going: the function Sītā performs in the stories is precisely the function this industry sells.

Read the myth again after the seats and it stops sounding ancient: The Rāmāyaṇa calls itself Rāma's story, but its moral engine is Sītā: every choice that matters is measured against her. The age changed. The work did not.
## The Method, Stated Plainly

None of this is numerology. A seat exists only where the match can be argued from the deity's documented domains and deeds — weighted, published, and falsifiable. The full derivation, the weights, and the challenge process are public on the [methodology page](/patterns/methodology/). If a seat in this file reads wrong, the atlas itself tells you how to prove it — and the correction becomes part of the record.
## For the Ones Who Work There

If you work in faith & spiritual organizations, wedding, family & maternity, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it. The [patron tier](/sites/sita/patron/) and the [advertising terms](/terms/advertising/) describe the mechanics; the resonance above describes the fit. The story is the pitch; the seats are just where it already works.
